purpose: silver_flights holds one row per scheduled flight segment departing a NYC-area airport (EWR, JFK, LGA) in the first half of 2013, carrying scheduling, actual timing, delay, distance, aircraft-registry, and airport-reference attributes.
usage: Read at the grain of one row per flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport. Actual-timing and delay columns (dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes) are null for roughly 3% of rows, consistent with cancellations or unrecorded operations, and must be handled as optional. Aircraft-registry columns (aircraft_manufacturer, aircraft_model, aircraft_manufacture_year, aircraft_seat_count, aircraft_engine_type) and destination-reference columns (dest_airport_name, dest_municipality, dest_iso_region, dest_elevation_ft, dest_longest_runway_ft) are null for 16%-17.7% and 2.1% of rows respectively, reflecting incomplete joins against external reference data, and consumers should treat absence as unknown rather than zero.
limitations: The profile cannot confirm that flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport is the true identifying grain beyond the observed row-level uniqueness (duplicate_row_rate 0.0); it awaits deterministic measurement. captured_at is retained pipeline load metadata, not flight data, and should not be used in flight-level analysis. The registry and destination-reference join gaps (aircraft_* at ~16%, dest_* at ~2.1%) are not explained by this profile and may reflect missing source coverage rather than data quality defects. is_cancelled's two boolean values are enforced by its declared type rather than an accepted_values_subset rule.
